doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

title: Elmira pleasure ground and photographs of sidemen
summary: They discuss Sunday picnics at Elmira pleasure ground, then identify Ernie Stevens, Emil Christian, Tony Parenti and others in photos.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: You mentioned the Elmira pleasure ground too. Did you play there? Yeah. Elmira's, yeah. Every Sunday.
What did they have there? Picnics or what?
Picnics, yeah. Yeah. And a regular open pavilion.

Regular open pavilion, just for the little stuff. Top on it, shed over it, you know. And Mr. Foster had the ballroom right across from the... Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
That's Mr. Stevens. What's his name again? Ernie Stevens?
Yeah, Ernie Stevens, yeah, right here. And that's his two sons. They were in the service, too. And this here is Emil Christian and Tony Parenti.
She's only keeping this stuff since we moved back in this place.
That's Brown, Lopez. This is Loyal Canna.
You know I must have had some dope ones. Oh, I'm telling you, I have it.
I mean, I have newspaper cut in school. He comes every now and then he comes in town, too. Yeah, I got his picture about 20 years ago.
You see, the thing is, you know, you got the pictures before you to show you that it must have been sold. Must have been sold.
You gave him the gold record, yeah.
